[SHEET 03.B] · THE TRAP

When a challenger closes the gap

In a survey of 16 great-power rivalries over 500 years, 12 ended in systemic war. [UNVERIFIED] Allison calls it the Thucydides Trap.

[SHEET 03.C] · FOUR IDEAS

One planet, different maps

[SHEET 03.D] · LIMIT

Where the cycle model strains

The overview lists four counter-theories to a smooth hegemonic cycle:

  • Keohane: institutions and shared standards keep cooperation going after dominance wanes.
  • Ikenberry: the American-led order is institutionally dense, with high exit costs, so its rules may outlast its dominance.
  • Nye: power is spread across a three-dimensional chessboard, which makes single-hegemon displacement models too simple.
  • Ferguson: empires are complex adaptive systems, and collapse can come abruptly within a decade.

Reconcile before launch: the overview’s section 7 says the cycles converge synchronously. The revised model (Rev C) says coupled, not synchronized. [REV 1 · OPEN]
